text:
marta: certwatcher fired an alert — keystore drift between apac-proxy and eu-proxy at ~03:20 UTC. apac shows 6 certs, eu shows 2. KMS decrypt errors in eu. :warning:
ryan: did we have any RBAC/iam changes last night? i remember a small rename around the keystore roles
olivia: i pulled logs, looks like: 
```
2026-03-21T03:19:58Z ERROR certwatcher eu-west1 cert_fetch failed: KMS_DECRYPT_DENIED key=projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/keystore-key
principal="serviceAccount:svc-certwatcher@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
```
sam: that principal lost the old binding. we renamed role keystore-reader->keystore-accessor in the last infra PR, and the terraform apply in eu failed on iam binding due to an API quota spike. i think certwatcher never got the new role in eu. :grimacing:
juan: confirming via audit logs. query i used: `gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName=\"google.iam.v1.IAM.CreateBinding\" AND resource.labels.project_id=\"redwood-prod\"" --freshness=7d` shows the rename at 2026-03-20T22:05:12Z and a subsequent failed apply at 22:07:01Z (eu).
marta: ok, mitigation steps i propose:
  1) temporarily rebind the legacy role keystore-reader to svc-certwatcher in eu project to restore decrypt ops (quick rollback). kubectl/kms commands below.
 2) re-run terraform apply with proper backoff / quota bump for eu region and ensure binding created.
 3) run certsync and monitor for successful decrypts, then rotate keystore if any certs were rewrapped.

sam: fast commands for step 1 (eu project):
```
# grant legacy role binding quickly
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \
  --member=serviceAccount:svc-certwatcher@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/keystoreReader
# then force certsync for eu proxies
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/certsync -- /bin/sh -c "./certsync --region=eu-west1 --force"
```
olivia: note — do NOT attempt to manually unwrap any wide-range keys unless we have a tracked ticket + exec window. if the key is symmetric and the service is supposed to decrypt, rebinding is safer than manual unwrap. sec-bot: please log this as an incident with tag: encryption-in-transit and include audit query.
sec-bot: INCIDENT_CREATED id=INC-2026-031-09 severity=high tags=[encryption-in-transit, keystore, eu] owner=@marta
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for certsync fix in eu started by @sam — canary=3 pods, rollout_id=roll-4723
juan: after rebind we should verify KMS metrics: `gcloud kms operations list --location=europe-west1 --filter="status=SUCCESS" --limit=50` and check for `Decrypt` ops from svc-certwatcher principal. also search audit log for `google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt` with that principal.
marta: done rebind at 03:27 UTC. immediate logs: 
```
03:27:15 INFO certsync eu-west1 attempt=1 decrypt=ok certs_synced=4
03:27:16 INFO certwatcher eu-west1 reload success routes_affected=non-critical:search,metrics
```
olivia: good — non-critical routes only. we should still harden so this doesn't reoccur:
  - ensure terraform apply has retries + quota-check for eu provider
  - add an alert for terraform-plan vs actual IAM bindings (drift detector)
  - require a preflight that validates service accounts referenced in iam bindings exist in target project

sam: also add an audit-logging lint check in CI: fail if an iam rename is present in PR without a matching change in per-region variable file.
juan: i archived the audit query and exported a CSV of the failed apply events to the incident ticket.
marta: postmortem plan: 1) roll back the rename (or make apply idempotent), 2) add terraform backoff + quota awareness, 3) add drift-detector alert and remediation playbook, 4) run a KMS access sweep for all region-local key usage and map principals -> roles.
olivia: tagging for compliance: @compliance please note — exposure window ~03:20–03:27 UTC, affected certs = 4 proxy certs in eu. we rebinded and verified decrypt success.
sec-bot: ACTIONS_ASSIGNED [marta: lead triage & postmortem, sam: infra terraform retry fixes, olivia: compliance pack & audit evidence, juan: create drift detection query] ETA=48h
ryan: thanks team — looks like we avoided any customer impact. please push the postmortem draft to #postmortems when ready. :thumbsup:
